scope: Short closed-loop B2 load on three existing Kubernetes hosts; one database per worker, one overwritten key per database, maintenance enabled.
limitations: No sustained-load, fixed-arrival overload, mixed-workload or latency SLO claim.
Final live values and revisions are verified; overwritten historical values and cold recovery are not checked by this workload.
Ten-second controller sampling can miss resource peaks; kubelet observations have their own timestamps. CPU intervals use those timestamps.
CPU averages include setup. RSS and working-set counters are different approximate measures.
The 32-database runs change both admission capacity and payload size; they do not isolate a causal throughput improvement. Database-to-partition mapping is randomized by the synthetic names.
Provider status/reason for kind=other uploads was not captured; no guess about the underlying cause.
No namespace-budget exhaustion, large key cardinality, hot-database contention, or mutually untrusted tenant fairness qualification.

workload.context: Three stock Kubernetes hosts; B2; native release image localhost:32000/durable-db@sha256:26588bf868b75a72fbc05d1f7a703c7e9c6b44e4367e7066cef3a9d1541e0219; see resources.json for limits and counters.
limitations: Small samples are descriptive, not an SLO guarantee.
Closed-loop load does not measure queue growth at a fixed arrival rate.
Provider request counts, billed storage, and cost are not measured.
Setup is excluded; retries, backoff, and failed operations are included in each measured phase.

harness_checks.local: SDK lost acknowledgements preserve exact request bodies; funding refusals and final counters are retained; Python syntax and site link checks pass.

funding_diagnosis.original_large_run: Six HTTP 413 responses were uncategorized. The focused repeat below identifies tenant funding exhaustion; it does not retroactively label each original response.
funding_diagnosis.result: All four writers refused with tenant_funding after 88 successful measured writes each. Each ledger allocated its full 64 MiB ceiling, including 32 MiB of funded maintenance reserve. Each reserve had claimed 873193 bytes across two checkpoint constructions. Namespace allocation was 40 MiB of its 1 GiB ceiling.
funding_diagnosis.interpretation: Admission charges conservative future rewrite contributions per transaction. Allocation/grants/reserve are not physical stored bytes or a provider bill. No quota was raised during any run.
funding_diagnosis.next: Reduce repeated prepayment for already-covered checkpoint rewrites while retaining durable funding and bounded retry charges; separately identify the provider status behind ambiguous upload failures.
